field_defs.label: Lamp used
field_defs.hint: Lamp type and power for each test (Test 2: small lamp, 25 to 40 W).

field_defs.label: Mains protection
field_defs.hint: Isolation transformer or GFCI, and the fuse value, for Tests 2 and 3.

field_defs.label: Power meter
field_defs.hint: Meter used for lamp power, or none (then the panel Isc is the light sensor).

field_defs.label: Panel temperature probe
field_defs.hint: Probe and where it sits on the panel, or none.

field_defs.label: Scope or logic analyser
field_defs.hint: Instrument used for Test 1, and the probe ground point (SELV side only).

field_defs.label: Pico firmware commit
field_defs.hint: Git commit of the Pico firmware. It must match the dimmer firmware (status frame of 9 bytes).

field_defs.label: Dimmer firmware commit
field_defs.hint: Git commit of the dimmer firmware.

field_defs.label: Operator
field_defs.hint: Name of the person running the session, and of the second person present for mains tests.

steps.title: Safety rules read
steps.instructions: Read hardware/dimmer/README.md and the safety part of docs/hardware_v1/dimmer_bench.md. A second person is present for Tests 2 and 3. There is a way to cut the mains. No lamp is ever on unattended. Pass: all true.

steps.section: Test 0: SELV only, no mains, no lamp
steps.title: Link, status and alpha read-back
steps.instructions: Run: uv run python3 scripts/dimmer_bench.py --only link --only alpha. Pass: link_ok true, mains and locked false, set angle read back, applied angle None.

steps.section: Test 0: SELV only, no mains, no lamp
steps.title: Link stable for a minute
steps.instructions: Run the stable check. Pass: link_ok stays true and no read fails. The bad frame counter is not sent to the Pi: it is checked in Test 1.

steps.section: Test 0: SELV only, no mains, no lamp
steps.title: Host, I2C and SPI timeouts and the dimmer deadman
steps.instructions: Run the host-timeout, i2c-unplug, spi-unplug and deadman checks. Pass: the Pico returns to 180 deg within about 3 s of a killed host, link_ok goes false within about 2 s of an unplugged I2C cable, the Pico stays at 180 deg after an SPI unplug. timed_out may be inconclusive (see the procedure). Write down the measured times.

steps.section: Test 0: SELV only, no mains, no lamp
steps.title: Limiter budget falls and rises
steps.instructions: Run the budget-fall and budget-rise checks. Pass: the budget falls about 1 s per second while the lamp is commanded on and rises about 1 s per second while off.

steps.section: Test 0: SELV only, no mains, no lamp
steps.title: Limiter trip, refusal and re-arm
steps.instructions: Run the trip and no-restart checks. Pass: tripped is set at the end of the budget (120 s from full), on-commands are refused, an early OFF is remembered, a stream of on-commands never restarts the dimmer, and it re-arms after the cool-down plus an OFF.

steps.section: Test 0: SELV only, no mains, no lamp
steps.title: Dimmer reset clears the limiter
steps.instructions: Run the reset-clears check. Pass: after a reset the budget is back to about 120 s and tripped is clear.

steps.section: Test 1: software I2C timing on the Pico board
steps.title: SCL frequency
steps.instructions: Measure the SCL frequency on GPIO6 with a scope or logic analyser (SELV side). Write down the value. Pass: about 100 kHz or lower, never above 100 kHz.

steps.section: Test 1: software I2C timing on the Pico board
steps.title: Start, stop and rise time
steps.instructions: Check the start and stop timing against the I2C standard mode limits and measure the rise time with the 4.7 kohm pull-ups. Pass: rise time below 1000 ns, start and stop timing inside the limits. Write down the values.

steps.section: Test 1: software I2C timing on the Pico board
steps.title: 10 minutes of status polling
steps.instructions: Poll the status for 10 minutes and read the bad frame counter on the dimmer USB log or on the logic analyser. Pass: the counter does not rise. Write down the count.

steps.section: Test 1: software I2C timing on the Pico board
steps.title: Old status frame after a skipped read
steps.instructions: Provoke a skipped status read and look at the next reads (see the procedure). Pass or fail: write down whether the status lags by one frame.

steps.section: Test 2: mains with a small lamp
steps.title: Bring-up order and protection
steps.instructions: Small lamp (25 to 40 W), isolation transformer or GFCI, fuse in line, second person ready to cut the plug. Follow the bring-up order in firmware/esp32c3-dimmer/README.md. Pass: all true.

steps.section: Test 2: mains with a small lamp
steps.title: Mains and lock
steps.instructions: Run: uv run python3 scripts/dimmer_bench.py --mains --only mains-lock. Pass: mains true and locked true. Also write down the mains frequency from the dimmer log (about 50 Hz).

steps.section: Test 2: mains with a small lamp
steps.title: Real alpha range
steps.instructions: Run the mains-range check. Pass: the applied angle is inside about 25 to 153 deg and equals the requested angle inside that range. Write down the applied angles.

steps.section: Test 2: mains with a small lamp
steps.title: Lamp power against alpha
steps.instructions: At 30, 60, 90, 120 and 150 deg, short windows, write down the lamp power from a power meter, or the panel Isc from a curve capture. Compare with lamp_power_fraction. Write down the values and the result.

steps.section: Test 2: mains with a small lamp
steps.title: Lamp dark at 180 and when the keepalive stops
steps.instructions: Run the mains-dark check and answer the question about the lamp. Pass: the lamp is dark at 180 deg and dark within about 4 s after the process is killed.

steps.section: Test 3: full halogen lamp with the panels
steps.title: Short windows with the full lamp
steps.instructions: Only after Test 2 passed. Use short windows (10 s or less) and a person watching. Pass: the lamp follows the angle, and the lamp is off after each window. Write down the window length and angle of each.

steps.section: Test 3: full halogen lamp with the panels
steps.title: Panel temperature before a window
steps.instructions: Record the panel temperature before each window, if a probe exists.

steps.section: Test 3: full halogen lamp with the panels
steps.title: Panel temperature after a window
steps.instructions: Record the panel temperature at the end of each window and again at 30 s, 60 s and 120 s after the lamp is off. This shows how fast the panels cool, and the limiter constants are tuned from it.

open_questions.text: Was there any unexpected behaviour during the session?
Do the numbers 120 s (trip) and 60 s (resume) fit the panel temperatures seen in Test 3? Write down the suggested values.
